title: Securities Trading (including Inside Information) Policy

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: Chairman of the relevant Dexus Board; distinguished only for approval (an Independent Director and the General Counsel).

tiers.name: Independent Director
tiers.description: Independent Directors of Dexus entities; distinguished only for approval (the Chairman, or another Independent Director during the Chairman's absence, and the General Counsel).

tiers.name: Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: CEO of the relevant Dexus entity; distinguished only for approval (the Chairman, or an Independent Director during absence, and the General Counsel).

tiers.name: Executive General Manager (including KMP)
tiers.description: Executive General Managers, including other Key Management Personnel; distinguished only for approval (the CEO and the Head of Governance).

tiers.name: Employee
tiers.description: All Employees of Dexus (a defined term collectively covering Directors, Employees including KMP, and Contractors & temporary employees); distinguished only for approval (the relevant Executive General Manager, or another EGM during absence, and the Head of Governance). All substantive prohibitions in section 7 (short-term trading, margin lending, hedging of unvested securities) apply without differentiation across this whole group.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Immediate family members, and people or entities (including SMSFs) over which the Employee may exert influence in investment decisions.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities

windows.start_anchor: day after half yearly and yearly results are announced to the market

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The CEO may cancel a trading window at any time, effective immediately on notification to all Employees, and may (in consultation with the Chair) identify additional trading windows, impose restrictions on trading in other financial products (e.g. where Dexus is party to a significant external transaction), or in exceptional circumstances restrict Listed Securities Funds from trading in DXS, ADI/DXI or DXC. Not stated to be confidential.

rules.detail: 'Dexus Securities' is defined only as the ASX-quoted DXS/ADI(DXI)/DXC stapled securities themselves, and the section 10 approval regime applies to 'listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus'. A third-party OTC derivative (such as a bank-written put/call) referencing Dexus Securities is arguably neither a Dexus Security nor a product managed by Dexus, so it is not clearly caught by the trading-window or Business Approval Table machinery; only the general Corporations Act insider trading prohibition on 'the relevant financial product' and the specific unvested-securities hedging ban would apply.
Absolute ban on entering into any transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging price exposure on securities that remain unvested under an equity plan.
rules.evidence: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities

rules.detail: Hedging of securities that have vested and ceased to be held under plan terms is not separately named; section 8 provides only that dealings in such securities 'must only occur in accordance with this Policy', which turns on whether the arrangement counts as 'trading in Dexus Securities' (see derivatives topic gap).

Monetisation is not named. It would fall within 'Deal' (apply for, acquire, dispose of, or enter into an agreement to do so) and within section 10's requirement that 'all trades ... in listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus require prior approval' if the arrangement is treated as trading in Dexus Securities, requiring approval per the Business Approval Table within a trading window.
rules.evidence: Deal in (i.e. apply for, acquire, dispose of or enter into an agreement to do so) the relevant financial product

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not named; the same scope gap as OTC derivatives generally applies (see derivatives topic).
Employees must not trade in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities; no tier or approval carve-out.
rules.evidence: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Dexus securities is not named outside the specific margin lending ban.

Only 'margin lending activities' are expressly banned; a broader secured financing or lending arrangement not structured as a margin loan (e.g. a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge of the shares) is not addressed.
Ban on trading Dexus securities for short term gain, defined as a purchase and sale within 30 days; no carve-out for plan securities is stated.
rules.evidence: trading in Dexus securities for short term gain (defined as a purchase and sale within 30 days)

exceptions.evidence: participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by Dexus (subject to insider trading provisions in the Corporation Act)

acquisition of Dexus securities through a distribution reinvestment plan; acquisition of Dexus securities through a security purchase plan available to all retail securityholders; acquisition of Dexus securities through a rights issue

exceptions.approver: CEO and/or Company Secretary (via referral to Head of Governance)
exceptions.evidence: Trading in financial products outside the trading windows may be granted in situations of severe financial hardship provided the Employee is not in possession of Inside Information.
This Policy does not apply to any fund that currently or in the future is established to trade in listed securities (Listed Securities Funds).

exemption_authority: Severe financial hardship exemption: request referred to the Head of Governance, approved by the CEO and/or Company Secretary if accompanied by sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action; if granted, notified in writing and the trade must be executed within 5 business days. The CEO in consultation with the Chair may also open additional windows or, in exceptional circumstances, restrict Listed Securities Funds' trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purpose of this Policy, reference to Dexus Securities includes reference to Dexus (ASX:DXS), Dexus Industria REIT (ASX:ADI) and Dexus Retail Convenience REIT (ASX:DXC). ... All trades by Employees in listed and unlisted financial products managed by Dexus require prior approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank-written OTC put/call over DXI units is not itself a Dexus Security nor a product managed by Dexus, so the trading-window and Business Approval Table machinery may not apply to the derivative legs at all, leaving only the general insider trading law and the unvested-securities hedging ban as constraints.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is confined to margin lending; a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge or charge over the collared shares, not structured as a margin loan, is not expressly prohibited by this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into a transaction or arrangement for the purpose of hedging exposure to movements in the price of un-vested securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging of vested Dexus securities is not restricted by this clause at all, so a collar can only be written once the incentive securities have vested and ceased to be held under the plan's terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where any approval is required for a dealing under this Policy, approval will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the Media Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even where the approval regime is found to apply, a bank-facing collar could be refused as a discretionary reputational matter regardless of legal compliance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where approval is withheld, the Employee is to keep that fact confidential and not disclose it to anyone. ... A clearance to trade may be withdrawn if circumstances change.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A granted clearance for collar execution can be revoked before completion and any refusal must be kept confidential, creating execution timing risk for the bank counterparty.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates of the above. An Associate would include immediate family members, people or entities (including SMSFs) over which the Employee may exert influence in investment decisions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through an SMSF or family member does not escape the Policy's approval regime, which the Business Approval Table expresses as applying to 'Person (including Associates)'.

summary: A funded collar is more plausible here than under a typical ASX policy because 'Dexus Securities' and the section 10 approval regime are defined by reference to products 'managed by Dexus', a term a third-party bank's OTC put/call over DXI units arguably does not satisfy, so the trading-window and Business Approval Table machinery may not apply to the derivative legs at all - leaving only the general insider trading prohibition and, while the units remain unvested, the express ban on hedging arrangements over unvested securities. Once the collared units have vested and ceased to be held under plan terms, ordinary dealing rules would likely apply if the arrangement is treated as 'trading in Dexus Securities': confined to the 28-day post-results and 14-day post-AGM windows, requiring written approval per the Business Approval Table, subject to a discretionary 'Media Test', with any refusal kept confidential and any granted clearance revocable before the trade (which must complete within 5 business days). The secured-financing prohibition is narrower than usual, banning only 'trading in Dexus securities as part of margin lending activities' rather than any secured financing arrangement, so a bespoke bank loan secured by pledge of the shares (not structured as a margin loan) is not expressly prohibited. Overall a funded collar on vested, unlocked units appears achievable outside a formal margin-loan structure, subject to whatever approval regime is found to apply and to the Media Test discretion.
